AIM Gun Certification

By: Sasha OLD | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
What if those working in security or in our police force didn't know how to operate their weapons?

Unique Selling Point:
We expose how one gun certification company - AIM - in Whiteriver near nelspruit is battling those who are forging his certificates. We will expose those who buy them, those who sell them, and actual gun training facilities that fraudulently sell AIM's firearm training certificates. This means that all of those people have not gone through the training of how to fire a gun and are a danger to themselves and everyone else.

Summary:
To break this down it means the training provider and all Firearm Instructors must be accredited with the SAPS and SASSETA / SAPFTC and all will carry certain unit standards that may be instructed, assessed and only then will a Proficiency certificate be issued by the relevant training accredited centre and also a SoR. The accredited training provider must also have his own accredited shooting range or access to such a range.

Further information:

5. During August 2018, the Dedicated Firearm Officer (DFO) from Bushbuckridge SAPS called my training centre to verify the validity of a person that submitted his application for a competency certificate. I requested him to scan and send me a copy of the training certificates that the person submitted. He did so. See attachment called Fraud 13.

6. Both the AIM and SAPFTC certificates were fraudulent. The following parts of information that can be verified from a certificate is as follows: a. The ID number on the certificate did not appear on our database. b. The AIM certificate number AIM/00467/2018 was not relevant to the number of trained individuals for the time. c. The SCV Number (AIM/467/2018) did not match the number below the barcode. This number is provided from the SAPFTC database and is different every time a SoR is printed. This unique barcode number that is reflected is P0299220882. This barcode number is allocated on the SAPFTC SoR as a person with ID number 8410175823080 Abraham Oubre Mathebula. He did train with AIM and received his legally printed certificates. d. The signature at the bottom of the certificate resembles that of one of my female instructors. This instructor is fully accredited with the SAPFTC and holds an Intermediate Level Instructors accreditation and is fully current with all rules and regulations as stipulated with the SAPFTC.

7. I reported this fraud to the DFO that requested the confirmation.

8. Another request came from the same DFO and we followed the same method to validate the certificate. a. The ID number 9201091019088 (Tshepiso Nonyana) was not trained by AIM. b. The unique barcode number was the same as above. c. The AIM certificate number was different from the previous, but does not reflect on our system.

9. See attachment called Fraud 12. 10. Another verification was requested and produced the same results. The ID number was 8901280944084 (Hedibone Monareng) was not trained by AIM. a. The unique barcode number was again as before. b. The AIM certificate number were different but was not on our system.

11. See attachment called Fraud 11.

12. It is at this time that I made an appointment with Lieutenant Colonel Mtimunye who is the Provincial DFO for Mpumalanga. At the meeting in his office I explained my frustration about the number of fraudulent certificates that is doing the rounds. His answer shocked me. He replied, “Chris I know of about six hundred (600) certificates in the province that is fraudulent, but what can I do?”

13. I suggested that I have gathered information of the possible source of these certificates. I asked that he sends somebody in there to buy a certificate “under cover” or a “mole”. He replied that he cannot do that because it will be “Entrapment” and will not stand in court.

14. He then suggested that I report this to Captain Ronel Bekker because she is the DFO at Nelspruit SAPS. It is in her jurisdiction and she must handle it.

15. I went to Nelspruit but could not meet with her because she was attending to other of her duties. I left the information with a lady in her office with the name of Lynette Rossouw.

16. During November 2018 I was called by a friend of mine. His name is Danie Theron. He was employed at Electra Communication in Jones street 20, Nelspruit. He asked me since when does a person with the name of Jurie Grobler work for AIM. I responded I know this person, but he never worked for me. Why?

17. He replied that Jurie sold AIM certificates to the lady in the reception and to other personnel as well. After he spoke to me, he told the lady that Jurie never worked for AIM. She then made contact with Jurie and he returned the money she paid, and she destroyed the fraudulent certificate. The ID number of Jurie Johannes Grobler is 7603145211086. Danie is willing to testify to this. Danie Theron’ s cell number is 0834489808.

18. I then went on to set up a meeting with one of the other people working at Elektra, who also bought from Jurie, but did not receive his certificate. The person is Michael Conrad de Beer with ID number 7703255061089.

19. The meeting was held in the boardroom at Electra on 12 November 2018. I indicated that the whole meeting will be recorded so I can submit it as evidence should it be necessary. Everybody agreed. The sound recording is available. 20. During the meeting after I established that Michael did indeed were waiting for certificates from Jurie. We at the meeting decided that Michael should phone Jurie and try and establish when he can expect the certificates he paid for. He did phone and on the first try Jurie did not answer. Jurie then phoned back and they discussed the matter about the outstanding certificates. It is all on the recording.

21. After the meeting I processed all events and decided that I must open a case at the Nelspruit SAPS to investigate this. The case number is CAS/703/11/2018.

22. At the time when Jurie was selling these certificates he was employed at Phoenix Security in Nelspruit. Another certificate that Jurie had issued was to a Rynhard du Toit with ID number 9708015023087. The fraudulent certificate is in my possession.

23. In January 2019 the verification of certificates intensified and seems to be out of control. All requests were verified by the same means as before. See attachments (10, 9,8,7,6 and 5).

24. On 10 January 2019 Mr. Shaderack Malitsha with ID 7304246008089 came to AIM for his Regulation 21 shoot. During this time, he realized that he was issued by a fraudulent certificate for training. He agreed to help us with information of where he got in contact with to buy this.

25. He indicated that he approached a security guard working at Phoenix security. This was at the Dyzenze shopping centre near the Numbi gate. He paid the money to the guard, and also collected it from him at the centre. See attachment Fraud Dyzenze.

26. On Friday 24 May 2019 I was called by a person called Syabonga and he requested the I print him a SoR, I requested a copy of his ID so I could verify. He said he trained with AIM, but I could not find his detail because the copy he sends me was unreadable. See Fraud 4. His cell number is 0768034476. It seems he thinks AIM has a training centre in the Malalane / Komatipoort area. AIM never had a centre in that area?

27. Certificates popped up from the Komatipoort / Malelane area. Apparently, certificates is also being issued at Shongwe Mission Hospital in that area. Person Thulani P Khoza bought a certificate from a person called Ester Lamahlalela. She then pays it to the “owner” called Mkhabela on cell number 0729216839 and also person Makuku as mention in paragraph 30 (c).

28. It now is clear that not only was Jurie selling certificates, but also the people in Nelspruit.

29. On 3 May 2019 I was called by my DFO in White River. He had an applicant that seemed to have a false certificate. The person is TT Mkhabela with ID number 9507315343082. He did his security grade training at a centre in Nelspruit called SNNN Security. It is here where he was given the opportunity to buy an AIM certificate. He did.

30. I had to step up the investigation. This time I got the Hawks involved. WO Sambo came to White River and conducted the interview and took the statement from the applicant. He provided us with the names, and photos of the two ladies in Nelspruit where he bought the certificates. They are:

a. Fakile on 0827015832 and b. Nomthandazo on 0793630529. c. They also have a person called Mr. Makukula on 0724321934. He sorts out the technical side of the certificates. He even gave us the Nedbank account number where he had to pay the money into!

31. Case number CAS/54/5/2019 was transferred from WO Sambo to Maj. I Olislager. I was notified by the SAPS by means of an SMS received on Wednesdat 05 June 2019 at 12:15.

32. The latest fraudulent certificate arrived at my office on Tuesday 11 June 2019 from the DFO in Acasia Pretoria North. See Fraud Acasia.

33. The long and the short here is that these unscrupulous people printing certificates, empower people to handle and use a firearm, even though they never had training of any kind. This is for normal applicants that want to buy a firearm, but mostly Security personnel working with firearms.

Press Release:


Illegal Gun Proficiency Certificates
Imagine a security guard who doesn’t know how to aim and fire a loaded weapon and firing his gun into the ground instead. In South Africa, it’s illegal to operate a firearm without proper training and the relevant proficiency certificate to prove it. Carte Blanche investigates some firearm training facilities in Mpumalanga selling fraudulent qualifications to people who’ve never been trained to use a weapon.
Producer: Sasha Schwendenwein
Presenter: Macfarlane Moleli
Research: Sinethemba Nogude
Watch the trailer


Script:


SOUNDUP: “YOU CAN’T SHOOT A GUN HERE, YOU SHOOT A GUN HERE!.”
Imagine a security guard who doesn’t know how to handle a firearm, and shoots into the ground?
SOUNDUP: GUN FIRES INTO GROUND.
YOU WOULD THINK THAT FIRING A GUN WOULD BE SOMETHING YOU WOULD WANT TO LEARN, ESPECIALLY IF YOU WANT TO BE IN SECURITY, OR TO PROTECT YOURSELF, BUT WE WILL SHOW THAT YOU CAN BUY A GUN PROFICIENCY CERTIFICATION AT A SHOPPING CENTRE…
A proficiency certificate is proof that you’ve completed a three to five day firearm training course which tests your knowledge of the firearms act: for example how to safely store and transport a firearm, the amount of ammunition you’re allowed to have in your possession; and when you can shoot in self-defense.
EVERYTHING YOU NEED TO KNOW ABOUT HOW TO HANDLE AND USE A FIREARM IS CONTAINED IN THIS BOOK WHICH WILL ASSESS YOUR KNOWLEDGE ON THE LAWS AND ON THE 4 DIFFERENT TYPES OF GUNS - HANDGUN, SHOTGUN, MANUAL RIFLE AND SEMI-AUTOMATIC. ONCE YOU PASS THE WRITTEN TEST THEN YOU ARE ALLOWED TO GO FOR THE PRACTICAL - AND THAT REQUIRES THE TRAINING CENTRE TO HAVE A SHOOTING RANGE…
Former police officer, Chris Botha opened Aim training academy in 2002 in White River near Nelspruit. He has since trained over 24,000 people to USE A FIREARM - and once they’ve passed his course, they can apply to be declared competent by the police.
Chris: “Once you receive your competency it means you can, in security, you can go and work with a firearm.”
Firearm instructor Zandile Mdhluli has worked for Botha for a decade, but their relationship was tested when Botha received a call from the local designated firearms officer, or DFO, THE POLICE OFFICER responsible for checking the legitimacy of competency requests.
Chris: “He said Chris, I've got an applicant that wants to apply for his SAPS competency but something looks fishy on the system.”
The certificate looked genuine because Mdhluli’s signature was on it, but when Chris checked the unique bar code on the website of the South African Professional Firearm Trainers Council - or PFTC….
Chris: “Sorry there is no such statement of results found.”
Mac: “This is how we know somebody has a fraudulent certificate.”
Chris: “That’s it.”
Zandile: “I was so shocked because my signature is not easy to forge.”
Botha laid fraud charges with Mpumalanga’s provincial DFO who, it turned out, was already aware of the problem.
Chris: “He knows of a large number of certificates that's fraudulent but what can he do about it?”
Botha received reports of fraudulent Aim certificates from police stations around the country. Meanwhile, Mdhluli was determined to clear her name.
Botha: "She got persistent because every time it's her signature.”
And her persistence led to “Princess,” who became a security guard after her husband was killed in an armed robbery. Desperation struck when her employer required her to become an armed guard, but gave her no time to complete the training.
Princess: “I don't want to lose my job, because I've got four kids.”
A colleague told her she could buy a certificate from a security training company in a Nelspruit shopping centre called SNNN training academy.
Princess: “I send the money to her account and then after two days they give me the certificate.”
Without ever picking up a gun, she received THIS certificate. Strangely, the name it bore was not SNNN but Botha’s trademark Aim Training Academy.
WITH THE HIGH UNEMPLOYMENT RATE, PEOPLE WANT JOBS AND SOMETIMES THE ONLY OPTION IS TO BE A SECURITY GUARD BUT EVEN THEN YOU NEED SOME FORM OF CERTIFICATION SO WHY TRAIN IF YOU CAN JUST PAY AND SECURE A JOB?
This is what Thulani Mkhabela had in mind, when he urgently needed firearm training to apply for a job in armed security. So he bought a certificate from SNNN.
Thulani: “It had my name, my identity number and the name of the company.”
Again, it was a fraudulent certificate in the name Aim Training Academy. Botha recruited Princess and Thulani to help the police investigate by handing over banking details and making statements. But months later, a seemingly easy case has yielded few results. So Botha decided to catch the criminals himself, with the help of an undercover operative we’ll call Peter.
Chris: “I want to buy an illegal aim training certificate as the owner of aim training.”
In this footage, Peter visits SNNN wearing a hidden camera. This employee gives him a choice.
Employee1: There are two ways to do it...You only get the certificate after you’ve been to a shooting range, but there are other ways you did say you know how to use a gun, so there is no problem...By later today you will have your certificate.”
Peter: “How much will it cost?”
Employee1: “R1800.”
Not only is SNNN not registered to give gun proficiency training, but as it’s in a mall it doesn’t even have a shooting range.
Peter: “I never even saw a gun. I didn't even produce my I.D.”
An hour later Peter returned to collect the certificate - which held a hidden surprise.
Mac: “So is this SNNN?”
Peter: “No it was Bosbok, but I went to SNNN, and then they gave me this one.”
Mac: “No man!”
Peter: “They say this is all legit. It's a different name of where I went to.”
This time the company name on the certificate was not Aim, but a different legitimate firearm training company - Bosbok. Owner Tobias Coetser says illegal certificates have caused the industry to question the Bosbok brand.
Tobias: “I’ve also got fraudulent certificates here at my office, this is dangerous putting a guy on the street with a firearm, with no knowledge of a firearm.”
ONCE YOU HAVE COMPLETED AND PASSED OUR FIREARM PROFICIENCY, TEST YOU THEN NEED TO TAKE YOUR CERTIFICATE TO YOUR NEAREST POLICE STATION THEY WILL DO A CRIMINAL AND A BACKGROUND CHECK AND IF ALL IS CLEAR, YOU ARE THEN DECLARED COMPETENT TO USE A FIREARM… BUT THAT’S ONLY IF THEY CHECK YOUR CERTIFICATE IS LEGITIMATE.
We checked and Peter’s Bosbok certificate wasn’t registered, so naturally he went back to SNNN. The employees told Peter to speak to their certificate source on the phone who said he must visit a local police station whose DFO wouldn’t verify the certificate.
Employee: “He has helped a lot of people... The person doesn’t come to check whether or not you went for training they just do it.”
Peter: “So it works at the Police station in Kabokweni?”(BLEEP)
Fikile: “When you go just say you’re there to register, don’t say anything else. They will then register you and process.”
As journalists we are not allowed to break the law and so, we couldn’t check if what SNNN was saying was true, but how many Peters have slipped through the system? Botha says to answer that question all you have to do is go to a shooting range during a gun refresher course - something all security personnel are legally required to do - like this security guard.
Mac: “Hey!!!!”
Chris: “She’s now just put in the magazine and she just pulling the trigger without cocking the gun… This is buying certificates, this person never saw the inside of a training centre.”
Mac: “HAHA Shes hitting the floor.”
And their grades reflect their incompetence.
Mac: There's people here that got 46 for his shooting average, and a 30. Are these people security guards?
Chris: “They’re all security guards. There’s a zero.”
Mac: “[Whistles…in shock]”
I went through some of the firearm safety steps with Botha, to experience what the practical side of gun proficiency training entails.
[Mac fires gun and get 100%]
Mac: “Looks like I’m better than most security guards!”
Then it was time to put some tough questions to SNNN…
Mac: “Do you guys have gun proficiency certificates here?”
Employee: Gun proficiency certificates?
Mac: “Yes.”
Employee: “No we don’t…we are not doing it yet.”
Mac: We had a person that has come in here and you gave them a gun proficiency certificate that said aim, and Bosbok, but you are SNNN?
Employee: “If you want to talk about the aim and the stuff, then I’m not the right person…
Mac: “Whose the right person?”
Employee: “The directors for this SNNN are currently not here.”
She then changed her story admitting SNNN had offered firearm training.
Employee: The reason that we stopped training people on firearm, is because the owner,failed to get a qualified instructor who is registered with the PFTC.”
Our producer called SNNN owner Susan Khoza who said it’s only a security training provider, not an accredited firearm training facility.
Susan: So we should send them to jail, those people.
Producer: So you’re not aware of it at all?
Susan: No they’re tarnishing my name, I’m telling you the truth, I’m not aware of anything.
But as the producer hung up, she got another call.
Khoza: “I am the owner of SNNN institute of security…”
Producer: What’s your name sorry?
Khosa: You speaking to Susan
Producer: To Susan.. Khoza?
Khosa: yes
Producer: no I’ve spoken to Susan Khoza, the owner of SNNN already, and your saying you’re also Susan Khoza…
Hangs up...
The real Susan Khoza was horrified to learn that someone was impersonating her.
Susan: “YOH!!! What kind of office is that?”
Producer: It’s your office at SNNN.
Ms. Khoza identified the two employees as Nancy Ngwenya and Fikile Lubisi. HER SISTERS who run her business. We called Nancy Ngwenya.
Producer: “Are you aware that SNNN is selling fraudulent certificates for firearm training?”
Nancy: “No SNNN does not train security officers for firearms…”
Sasha: “Are you impersonating Susan Khoza?”
Nancy: “No, why should I do that?”
In subsequent phone calls Ngwenya dismissed the allegations.
Nancy: “It’s not a denial, it is something we don’t do…”
Producer: “Even though we have it on undercover camera that you do?”
Nancy: “You can go ahead, we don’t have anything to hide.”
Fikile Lubisi also denied the allegation.
Soundup: “Producer: “Hi Fikile...are you selling illegal proficiency certificates?
Fikile: “No, no, no.”
PFTC Chairman Mac McGuire says those who buy certificates should also be held responsible.
Mac: “You're aware that what you're doing is a criminal act. You cannot convince me that you really didn't consider the fact that this is a little strange, you pay money, and you get given a certificate?”
The PFTC cannot shut down unregistered facilities, but wants to improve the authentication process. Meanwhile, government is responding to the rise in violent crime by planning to change gun legislation by clamping down on the security industry’s access to militarized guns.
Mac: “They’re saying that only shotguns and non semi-automatic weapons may be used, that means that your security officer that comes to your house, they now have to use revolvers again or pump action shotguns which takes away their ability. You don't want to go into a fight with an AK 47 with a revolver.”
Mpumalanga police spokesperson, Brigadier Leonard Hlathi says Botha’s cases are being investigated by senior detectives.
Hlathi: “We need to work together to be able to stop these guys, because definitely we’re sliding into a lawless element accessing firearms.”
SNNN alleged that some police stations don’t check the legitimacy of these firearm certificates. Hlathi says they will go back and recheck them.
THE MOST FRIGHTENING THING IN ALL OF THIS, IS THAT IF POLICE DO NOT CHECK PROPERLY THEN...
...untrained security guards can fire weapons in public places where they’re just as likely to hurt themselves or those they’re meant to protect. 12:09

nombuso@carteblanche.co.za 23 July 2019 Press Release: Illegal Gun Proficiency Certificates Imagine a security guard who doesn’t know how to aim and fire a loaded weapon and firing his gun into the ground instead. In South Africa, it’s illegal to operate a firearm without proper training and the relevant proficiency certificate to prove it. Carte Blanche investigates some firearm training facilities in Mpumalanga selling fraudulent qualifications to people who’ve never been trained to use a weapon. Producer: Sasha Schwendenwein Presenter: Macfarlane Moleli Research: Sinethemba Nogude Watch the trailer Script: SOUNDUP: “YOU CAN’T SHOOT A GUN HERE, YOU SHOOT A GUN HERE!.” Imagine a security guard who doesn’t know how to handle a firearm, and shoots into the ground? SOUNDUP: GUN FIRES INTO GROUND. YOU WOULD THINK THAT FIRING A GUN WOULD BE SOMETHING YOU WOULD WANT TO LEARN, ESPECIALLY IF YOU WANT TO BE IN SECURITY, OR TO PROTECT YOURSELF, BUT WE WILL SHOW THAT YOU CAN BUY A GUN PROFICIENCY CERTIFICATION AT A SHOPPING CENTRE… A proficiency certificate is proof that you’ve completed a three to five day firearm training course which tests your knowledge of the firearms act: for example how to safely store and transport a firearm, the amount of ammunition you’re allowed to have in your possession; and when you can shoot in self-defense. EVERYTHING YOU NEED TO KNOW ABOUT HOW TO HANDLE AND USE A FIREARM IS CONTAINED IN THIS BOOK WHICH WILL ASSESS YOUR KNOWLEDGE ON THE LAWS AND ON THE 4 DIFFERENT TYPES OF GUNS - HANDGUN, SHOTGUN, MANUAL RIFLE AND SEMI-AUTOMATIC. ONCE YOU PASS THE WRITTEN TEST THEN YOU ARE ALLOWED TO GO FOR THE PRACTICAL - AND THAT REQUIRES THE TRAINING CENTRE TO HAVE A SHOOTING RANGE… Former police officer, Chris Botha opened Aim training academy in 2002 in White River near Nelspruit. He has since trained over 24,000 people to USE A FIREARM - and once they’ve passed his course, they can apply to be declared competent by the police. Chris: “Once you receive your competency it means you can, in security, you can go and work with a firearm.” Firearm instructor Zandile Mdhluli has worked for Botha for a decade, but their relationship was tested when Botha received a call from the local designated firearms officer, or DFO, THE POLICE OFFICER responsible for checking the legitimacy of competency requests. Chris: “He said Chris, I've got an applicant that wants to apply for his SAPS competency but something looks fishy on the system.” The certificate looked genuine because Mdhluli’s signature was on it, but when Chris checked the unique bar code on the website of the South African Professional Firearm Trainers Council - or PFTC…. Chris: “Sorry there is no such statement of results found.” Mac: “This is how we know somebody has a fraudulent certificate.” Chris: “That’s it.” Zandile: “I was so shocked because my signature is not easy to forge.” Botha laid fraud charges with Mpumalanga’s provincial DFO who, it turned out, was already aware of the problem. Chris: “He knows of a large number of certificates that's fraudulent but what can he do about it?” Botha received reports of fraudulent Aim certificates from police stations around the country. Meanwhile, Mdhluli was determined to clear her name. Botha: "She got persistent because every time it's her signature.” And her persistence led to “Princess,” who became a security guard after her husband was killed in an armed robbery. Desperation struck when her employer required her to become an armed guard, but gave her no time to complete the training. Princess: “I don't want to lose my job, because I've got four kids.” A colleague told her she could buy a certificate from a security training company in a Nelspruit shopping centre called SNNN training academy. Princess: “I send the money to her account and then after two days they give me the certificate.” Without ever picking up a gun, she received THIS certificate. Strangely, the name it bore was not SNNN but Botha’s trademark Aim Training Academy. WITH THE HIGH UNEMPLOYMENT RATE, PEOPLE WANT JOBS AND SOMETIMES THE ONLY OPTION IS TO BE A SECURITY GUARD BUT EVEN THEN YOU NEED SOME FORM OF CERTIFICATION SO WHY TRAIN IF YOU CAN JUST PAY AND SECURE A JOB? This is what Thulani Mkhabela had in mind, when he urgently needed firearm training to apply for a job in armed security. So he bought a certificate from SNNN. Thulani: “It had my name, my identity number and the name of the company.” Again, it was a fraudulent certificate in the name Aim Training Academy. Botha recruited Princess and Thulani to help the police investigate by handing over banking details and making statements. But months later, a seemingly easy case has yielded few results. So Botha decided to catch the criminals himself, with the help of an undercover operative we’ll call Peter. Chris: “I want to buy an illegal aim training certificate as the owner of aim training.” In this footage, Peter visits SNNN wearing a hidden camera. This employee gives him a choice. Employee1: There are two ways to do it...You only get the certificate after you’ve been to a shooting range, but there are other ways you did say you know how to use a gun, so there is no problem...By later today you will have your certificate.” Peter: “How much will it cost?” Employee1: “R1800.” Not only is SNNN not registered to give gun proficiency training, but as it’s in a mall it doesn’t even have a shooting range. Peter: “I never even saw a gun. I didn't even produce my I.D.” An hour later Peter returned to collect the certificate - which held a hidden surprise. Mac: “So is this SNNN?” Peter: “No it was Bosbok, but I went to SNNN, and then they gave me this one.” Mac: “No man!” Peter: “They say this is all legit. It's a different name of where I went to.” This time the company name on the certificate was not Aim, but a different legitimate firearm training company - Bosbok. Owner Tobias Coetser says illegal certificates have caused the industry to question the Bosbok brand. Tobias: “I’ve also got fraudulent certificates here at my office, this is dangerous putting a guy on the street with a firearm, with no knowledge of a firearm.” ONCE YOU HAVE COMPLETED AND PASSED OUR FIREARM PROFICIENCY, TEST YOU THEN NEED TO TAKE YOUR CERTIFICATE TO YOUR NEAREST POLICE STATION THEY WILL DO A CRIMINAL AND A BACKGROUND CHECK AND IF ALL IS CLEAR, YOU ARE THEN DECLARED COMPETENT TO USE A FIREARM… BUT THAT’S ONLY IF THEY CHECK YOUR CERTIFICATE IS LEGITIMATE. We checked and Peter’s Bosbok certificate wasn’t registered, so naturally he went back to SNNN. The employees told Peter to speak to their certificate source on the phone who said he must visit a local police station whose DFO wouldn’t verify the certificate. Employee: “He has helped a lot of people... The person doesn’t come to check whether or not you went for training they just do it.” Peter: “So it works at the Police station in Kabokweni?”(BLEEP) Fikile: “When you go just say you’re there to register, don’t say anything else. They will then register you and process.” As journalists we are not allowed to break the law and so, we couldn’t check if what SNNN was saying was true, but how many Peters have slipped through the system? Botha says to answer that question all you have to do is go to a shooting range during a gun refresher course - something all security personnel are legally required to do - like this security guard. Mac: “Hey!!!!” Chris: “She’s now just put in the magazine and she just pulling the trigger without cocking the gun… This is buying certificates, this person never saw the inside of a training centre.” Mac: “HAHA Shes hitting the floor.” And their grades reflect their incompetence. Mac: There's people here that got 46 for his shooting average, and a 30. Are these people security guards? Chris: “They’re all security guards. There’s a zero.” Mac: “[Whistles…in shock]” I went through some of the firearm safety steps with Botha, to experience what the practical side of gun proficiency training entails. [Mac fires gun and get 100%] Mac: “Looks like I’m better than most security guards!” Then it was time to put some tough questions to SNNN… Mac: “Do you guys have gun proficiency certificates here?” Employee: Gun proficiency certificates? Mac: “Yes.” Employee: “No we don’t…we are not doing it yet.” Mac: We had a person that has come in here and you gave them a gun proficiency certificate that said aim, and Bosbok, but you are SNNN? Employee: “If you want to talk about the aim and the stuff, then I’m not the right person… Mac: “Whose the right person?” Employee: “The directors for this SNNN are currently not here.” She then changed her story admitting SNNN had offered firearm training. Employee: The reason that we stopped training people on firearm, is because the owner,failed to get a qualified instructor who is registered with the PFTC.” Our producer called SNNN owner Susan Khoza who said it’s only a security training provider, not an accredited firearm training facility. Susan: So we should send them to jail, those people. Producer: So you’re not aware of it at all? Susan: No they’re tarnishing my name, I’m telling you the truth, I’m not aware of anything. But as the producer hung up, she got another call. Khoza: “I am the owner of SNNN institute of security…” Producer: What’s your name sorry? Khosa: You speaking to Susan Producer: To Susan.. Khoza? Khosa: yes Producer: no I’ve spoken to Susan Khoza, the owner of SNNN already, and your saying you’re also Susan Khoza… Hangs up... The real Susan Khoza was horrified to learn that someone was impersonating her. Susan: “YOH!!! What kind of office is that?” Producer: It’s your office at SNNN. Ms. Khoza identified the two employees as Nancy Ngwenya and Fikile Lubisi. HER SISTERS who run her business. We called Nancy Ngwenya. Producer: “Are you aware that SNNN is selling fraudulent certificates for firearm training?” Nancy: “No SNNN does not train security officers for firearms…” Sasha: “Are you impersonating Susan Khoza?” Nancy: “No, why should I do that?” In subsequent phone calls Ngwenya dismissed the allegations. Nancy: “It’s not a denial, it is something we don’t do…” Producer: “Even though we have it on undercover camera that you do?” Nancy: “You can go ahead, we don’t have anything to hide.” Fikile Lubisi also denied the allegation. Soundup: “Producer: “Hi Fikile...are you selling illegal proficiency certificates? Fikile: “No, no, no.” PFTC Chairman Mac McGuire says those who buy certificates should also be held responsible. Mac: “You're aware that what you're doing is a criminal act. You cannot convince me that you really didn't consider the fact that this is a little strange, you pay money, and you get given a certificate?” The PFTC cannot shut down unregistered facilities, but wants to improve the authentication process. Meanwhile, government is responding to the rise in violent crime by planning to change gun legislation by clamping down on the security industry’s access to militarized guns. Mac: “They’re saying that only shotguns and non semi-automatic weapons may be used, that means that your security officer that comes to your house, they now have to use revolvers again or pump action shotguns which takes away their ability. You don't want to go into a fight with an AK 47 with a revolver.” Mpumalanga police spokesperson, Brigadier Leonard Hlathi says Botha’s cases are being investigated by senior detectives. Hlathi: “We need to work together to be able to stop these guys, because definitely we’re sliding into a lawless element accessing firearms.” SNNN alleged that some police stations don’t check the legitimacy of these firearm certificates. Hlathi says they will go back and recheck them. THE MOST FRIGHTENING THING IN ALL OF THIS, IS THAT IF POLICE DO NOT CHECK PROPERLY THEN... ...untrained security guards can fire weapons in public places where they’re just as likely to hurt themselves or those they’re meant to protect. 12:09

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): What if those working in security or in our police force didn't know how to operate their weapons?
metadata.Unique Selling Point: We expose how one gun certification company - AIM - in Whiteriver near nelspruit is battling those who are forging his certificates. We will expose those who buy them, those who sell them, and actual gun training facilities that fraudulently sell AIM's firearm training certificates. This means that all of those people have not gone through the training of how to fire a gun and are a danger to themselves and everyone else.
metadata.Summary: To break this down it means the training provider and all Firearm Instructors must be accredited with the SAPS and SASSETA / SAPFTC and all will carry certain unit standards that may be instructed, assessed and only then will a Proficiency certificate be issued by the relevant training accredited centre and also a SoR. The accredited training provider must also have his own accredited shooting range or access to such a range.

The latest fraudulent certificate arrived at my office on Tuesday 11 June 2019 from the DFO in Acasia Pretoria North. See Fraud Acasia. 33. The long and the short here is that these unscrupulous people printing certificates, empower people to handle and use a firearm, even though they never had training of any kind. This is for normal applicants that want to buy a firearm, but mostly Security personnel working with firearms.
